title: Pageviews vs Events: Which Should You Track?
description: When pageview analytics is enough, when you need custom events, and how that choice maps to privacy tools vs GA4 vs product analytics.
quickAnswer: **Pageviews** answer traffic questions: how many visits, from where, to which URLs. **Custom events** answer action questions: signups, upgrades, feature use. Most marketing sites start with pageviews; SaaS products usually need events.

sections.title: Two different questions
sections.content:
**Pageview analytics** asks: *What content did people see, and how did they arrive?*

**Event analytics** asks: *What did people do that matters to the business or product?*

Both can live in one tool (GA4, PostHog). Many privacy-first tools intentionally stay closer to pageviews and simple goals so the product stays light and compliant.

sections.title: When pageviews are enough
sections.content:
Stay pageview-first when:

- You run a **blog, docs site, or marketing site**
- Success metrics are traffic, referrers, and a few conversion goals (signup click, contact form)
- You want **privacy-first, lightweight** analytics without a big event taxonomy

Plausible and Fathom are built for this lane. You can still fire custom events for key buttons — just do not expect full product analytics depth.

sections.title: When you need custom events
sections.content:
Invest in events when:

- Users have **accounts** and multi-step journeys inside an app
- You care about **activation, retention, feature adoption**, or experiments
- Revenue happens through **instrumented purchases** you need to attribute precisely

That is the PostHog / mature GA4 lane. Expect engineering time for naming, identity, and QA — not just a script paste.

sections.title: Billing and volume gotchas
sections.content:
How you are charged changes the incentives:

- **Pageview tiers** (Plausible, Fathom hosted) — more pages ≈ more cost; custom events are usually secondary
- **Event volume** (PostHog Cloud, GA4 collection limits) — autocapture and chatty SDKs can burn quota
- **Session caps** (Hotjar) — recordings are not the same unit as pageviews

Use our [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/) with the unit your shortlist actually bills on.

sections.title: A practical rule of thumb
sections.content:
If your weekly meeting stares at **referrers and top pages**, start with a privacy-first web analytics tool.

If your weekly meeting stares at **funnels and retention charts**, start with product analytics (and optionally keep a lightweight tool on the marketing site).

New to the vocabulary? Read [Analytics Events: What They Are and Why They Matter](/learn/what-are-analytics-events/) next, then pick a comparison that matches your shortlist.
